the best configuration of our terminology extraction approaches is able to extract a large amount of relevant aspects, but that it also tends to extract many irrelevant aspects, which makes the task of filtering the most relevant ones a challenging one.

the best configuration of a terminology extraction approach for product aspect detection in customer reviews is a configuration that uses a term extraction method that combines both term frequency and document frequency information and uses a filtering technique that removes terms that appear in a small number of documents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a combination of term acquisition heurists, filtering techniques, and variant aggregation methods can improve the quality of the extracted terminology, which in turn can lead to improved performance of aspect-based review summarization systems.
we have shown that the problem of product aspect detection in customer reviews is well-suited to be cast as a terminology extraction task and that there is room for further improvement.

, for the task of product aspect detection, the best approach is one that combines the best of both worlds: a term acquisition method that is able to capture a wide range of product aspects (such as a statistical term acquisition method), and an aggregation technique that is able to reduce noise and focus on the most relevant product aspects (such a clustering technique).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of terminology extraction methods can be improved by carefully tuning the parameters of the employed algorithms and by combining multiple methods in a single framework.
the performance of the different approaches varies significantly depending on the dataset.
, in the terminology extraction approach, the use of a relevance measure that considers the frequency of a term in the corpus is crucial for obtaining a good performance.
